change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern: Fig. 7 does not match its legend or the Results text, so the LSD1 siRNA migration statement is unsupported. It also notes an apparent vertical discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot between the 293T and A549 lanes. It says similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The issues are unresolved because the authors did not respond, and the paper's abstract claims that LSD1 siRNA or pargyline suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites [12] for the H460 scratch-assay result and takes this knockdown result as the clearest sign that LSD1 drives migration, and the paper does report that result. The notice says the Fig. 7 results do not match the legend or the Results text, and that similarities with other groups' work question the validity and provenance of the results, so the evidence behind Aim 2's rationale is shaky. Your Section 2 cites [12] for LSD1 being higher in lung cancer tissue, which the paper reports. The notice does not name the tissue results, so it is unclear whether this background use is touched. Overall the impact is medium: the main hit is the Section 3 rationale, while the plan's own experiments do not depend on the paper's data.
recommendation: Your Section 3 cites [12] for the H460 scratch-assay result and takes this knockdown result as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration. The notice says the Fig. 7 results do not correspond to the Figure legend or the Results text, and that similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Hedge that sentence, cite the Expression of Concern, and rest Aim 2's rationale on other sources rather than this result. Your Section 2 cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue from 80 NSCLC patients, but the notice does not name those results, so keep it with a note and check it against other studies.
